admission-controller.md.title: Admission Controller
admission-controller.md.summary: An Admission Controller is a piece of code that intercepts requests to the Kubernetes API server before an object is persisted. These controllers can be validating, mutating, or both, and can reject or modify requests.

admission-policies.md.title: Validating and Mutating Admission Policies
admission-policies.md.summary: This document explains declarative admission policies in Kubernetes, detailing Validating and Mutating policies, their structure, and how they use the Common Expression Language (CEL). It covers the different policy types and binding mechanisms.

admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.title: Good Practices for Admission Webhooks in Kubernetes
admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.summary: This document outlines best practices for designing and implementing admission webhooks in Kubernetes. It covers considerations for performance, preventing loops, managing scope, and ensuring idempotence.

affinity.md.title: Kubernetes Affinity Rules
affinity.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes affinity, which are rules used to guide the scheduler on where to place pods. It details the two main types of affinity and how they are defined using labels and selectors.

aggregation-layer.md.title: Aggregation Layer
aggregation-layer.md.summary: The aggregation layer allows users to install additional Kubernetes-style APIs in a cluster. This is achieved by adding `APIService` objects to claim a specific URL path in the Kubernetes API.

annotation.md.title: Annotation Metadata
annotation.md.summary: This document explains what an annotation is, defining it as a key-value pair used to attach arbitrary, non-identifying metadata to objects. It details that this metadata can be small, large, structured, or unstructured.

api-group.md.title: Kubernetes API Group
api-group.md.summary: An API group is a set of related paths within the Kubernetes API. It is used to simplify the extension of the Kubernetes API by allowing users to enable or disable specific groups.

api-resource.md.title: Kubernetes API Resource Definition
api-resource.md.summary: This document defines what an API resource is within the Kubernetes type system. It explains that a resource corresponds to an endpoint on the Kubernetes API server and defines the schema for objects or operations.

api-server-bypass-risks.md.title: Kubernetes API Server Bypass Risks
api-server-bypass-risks.md.summary: This document describes ways security controls within the Kubernetes API server can be bypassed. It focuses on risks associated with static pods and the kubelet API, advising operators on necessary restrictions.

app-container.md.title: Application Containers in Pods
app-container.md.summary: This document explains what application containers are within a pod and how they relate to init containers. It clarifies the role of init containers in separating initialization tasks from the main application workload.

application-architect.md.title: Application Architect Role
application-architect.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Application Architect, who is responsible for the high-level design of an application. The architect ensures the implementation allows for scalable and maintainable interaction with surrounding components.

application-security-checklist.md.title: Application Security Checklist
application-security-checklist.md.summary: This document provides a checklist of basic guidelines for securing applications running in Kubernetes from a developer's perspective. It covers recommendations for application design, service accounts, and container security contexts.

approver.md.title: Approver Role Definition
approver.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Approver, who reviews and approves Kubernetes code contributions. Approval involves a holistic acceptance covering compatibility, conventions, performance, and system interactions.

architecture.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture
architecture.md.summary: This document outlines the necessary components for a complete Kubernetes cluster, detailing the roles of the control plane and worker nodes. It explains how these components work together to manage workloads and maintain cluster functionality.

authentication-mechanisms.md.title: Hardening Guide - Authentication Mechanisms
authentication-mechanisms.md.summary: This document guides users on selecting and securing appropriate authentication mechanisms for a Kubernetes cluster. It details the pros and cons of various built-in methods to help users choose the best security approach.

authorization.md.title: Kubernetes Authorization Mechanism
authorization.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes authorization works by evaluating request attributes against configured policies. Access is denied by default, and decisions are made sequentially by authorization modules.

autoscaling.md.title: Autoscaling Workloads
autoscaling.md.summary: This document explains how workloads in Kubernetes can be scaled based on resource demand. It details horizontal scaling using HPA and vertical scaling using VPA.

cadvisor.md.title: cAdvisor Overview
cadvisor.md.summary: cAdvisor is a daemon that collects, aggregates, and exports information about running containers. It provides users with insights into resource usage, performance characteristics, and network statistics for containers.

cdi.md.title: Container Device Interface (CDI)
cdi.md.summary: The Container Device Interface (CDI) is a specification defining how devices are configured inside containers. It works with device plugins and Dynamic Resource Allocation to provide workloads with necessary device setups like bind mounts or environment variables.

cel.md.title: Common Expression Language (CEL)
cel.md.summary: This document describes the Common Expression Language (CEL), a general-purpose, fast, portable, and safe expression language. It explains how CEL is used in Kubernetes for querying and fine-grained filtering.

certificate.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Certificate
certificate.md.summary: This document explains what a certificate is in the context of a Kubernetes cluster. It details how certificates are used to cryptographically secure access to the Kubernetes API for applications.

cgroup.md.title: cgroup (control group)
cgroup.md.summary: cgroup is a Linux kernel feature that allows for the resource isolation, accounting, and limiting of resource usage for groups of processes. It manages CPU, memory, disk I/O, and network usage.

cidr.md.title: CIDR Notation in Networking
cidr.md.summary: This document explains CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing), a notation used for describing IP address blocks. It details how CIDR is applied in Kubernetes to assign IP addresses to Nodes and Pods.

cla.md.title: Contributor License Agreement (CLA)
cla.md.summary: This document outlines the terms under which a contributor grants a license to an open-source project for their contributions. CLAs are used to resolve legal disputes regarding contributed material and intellectual property.

cloud-controller-manager.md.title: Cloud Controller Manager
cloud-controller-manager.md.summary: The Cloud Controller Manager is a Kubernetes control plane component that embeds cloud-specific control logic. It links a Kubernetes cluster to a cloud provider's API, separating cloud interaction logic from core cluster components.

cloud-native-security.md.title: Cloud Native Security and Kubernetes
cloud-native-security.md.summary: This document explains cloud-native information security principles applied across the development, distribution, and deployment lifecycle phases. It outlines security practices for building and deploying secure cloud-native platforms.

cloud-provider.md.title: Cloud Provider Definition
cloud-provider.md.summary: This document defines what a cloud provider is and explains the different types of cloud services they offer. It distinguishes between Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS) offerings.

cluster-administration.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Administration Overview
cluster-administration.md.summary: This document provides an overview for creating and administering Kubernetes clusters. It guides users through planning, managing, securing the cluster, and understanding necessary components.

cluster-operations.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Operations
cluster-operations.md.summary: This document outlines the work involved in managing a Kubernetes cluster, covering day-to-day operations and coordinating upgrades. It lists examples of cluster operations such as scaling, upgrades, and security implementation.

cluster-operator.md.title: Cluster Operator Role
cluster-operator.md.summary: This document defines the role of a Cluster Operator, which is responsible for configuring, controlling, and monitoring clusters. It clarifies that this role involves maintaining cluster uptime through maintenance and upgrades.

cluster.md.title: Cluster Definition
cluster.md.summary: This document defines a cluster as a set of worker machines (nodes) that run containerized applications. It explains the roles of worker nodes and the control plane in managing the application workload.

cncf.md.title: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
cncf.md.summary: The CNCF builds sustainable ecosystems and a community around projects that orchestrate containers in microservices architectures. Kubernetes is a key project within the CNCF, aiming to make cloud native computing ubiquitous.

cni.md.title: Container Network Interface (CNI)
cni.md.summary: This document introduces Container Network Interface (CNI) plugins, which are network plugins that follow the appc/CNI specification. It provides a foundational explanation of what CNI is within the context of container networking.

components.md.title: Kubernetes Components Overview
components.md.summary: This document provides a high-level overview of the essential components that constitute a Kubernetes cluster. It explains the roles of the control plane, node components, and optional addons.

condition.md.title: Kubernetes Resource Conditions
condition.md.summary: This document explains what a condition is in Kubernetes, detailing how it serves as a field in a resource's status to describe its current state. Conditions use a type, status (True, False, or Unknown), and optional fields to communicate resource status.

configuration.md.title: Kubernetes Configuration Mechanisms
configuration.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes separates configuration from code using APIs like ConfigMaps and Secrets. It also details methods for injecting configuration into workloads via sidecar or init containers.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables
container-env-variables.md.summary: This document explains what container environment variables are and their purpose within containers running in a pod. They provide necessary information and details about the container and its related cluster resources.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime
container-runtime.md.summary: The container runtime is a fundamental component that enables Kubernetes to effectively run containers. It is responsible for managing the execution and lifecycle of containers within the Kubernetes environment.

container.md.title: Container Definition
container.md.summary: This document defines a container as a lightweight, portable executable image containing software and its dependencies. It explains how containers decouple applications from the host infrastructure for easier deployment and scaling.

containerd.md.title: containerd overview
containerd.md.summary: containerd is a container runtime designed for simplicity, robustness, and portability. It functions as a daemon to handle tasks like fetching images, executing containers, and managing network access.

containers.md.title: Containers and Container Images
containers.md.summary: This document explains the concepts of containers, container images, and container runtimes. It details how containers decouple applications from infrastructure and the principles of immutable container images.

contributor.md.title: Contributor Definition
contributor.md.summary: This document defines what a 'Contributor' is within the Kubernetes project or community. It outlines the types of contributions individuals can make to the project.

control-plane.md.title: Control Plane
control-plane.md.summary: The Control Plane is the container orchestration layer responsible for exposing APIs and interfaces to define, deploy, and manage the lifecycle of containers. It is composed of various components that manage the orchestration process.

cpu-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configure Minimum and Maximum CPU Constraints for a Namespace
cpu-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to set minimum and maximum CPU resource constraints for Pods within a Kubernetes namespace using a LimitRange object. It details the steps to create the namespace, the LimitRange, and how Pods must adhere to these defined limits.

cpu-default-namespace.md.title: Configure Default CPU Requests and Limits for a Namespace
cpu-default-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to configure default CPU requests and limits for a Kubernetes namespace using a LimitRange. It details how the control plane applies these defaults to Pods that do not specify their own resource requests or limits.

cri-o.md.title: CRI-O Overview
cri-o.md.summary: CRI-O is a tool that enables the use of OCI container runtimes with Kubernetes CRI. It allows Kubernetes to utilize any OCI-compliant runtime for running Pods and fetching container images from remote registries.

cron-jobs.md.title: CronJob Documentation
cron-jobs.md.summary: This document explains what a CronJob is, how it creates scheduled jobs, and the syntax used to define their execution schedules. It details the structure and limitations of CronJobs.

csi.md.title: Container Storage Interface (CSI)
csi.md.summary: The Container Storage Interface (CSI) defines a standard interface for exposing storage systems to containers. It allows vendors to create custom storage plugins for Kubernetes as out-of-tree plugins.

customresourcedefinition.md.title: CustomResourceDefinition (CRD)
customresourcedefinition.md.summary: A CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) is an API object used to define a new custom API to extend the Kubernetes API server. It allows users to extend the built-in API resources when standard resources are insufficient.

daemonset.md.title: DaemonSet
daemonset.md.summary: A DaemonSet ensures that a copy of a Pod runs on every (or selected) Node in the cluster. It explains how DaemonSets are used for running node-level services like storage or logging daemons.

debug-application.md.title: Troubleshooting Applications
debug-application.md.summary: This document provides resources for fixing issues with containerized applications. It covers common problems with Kubernetes resources, interpreting container termination messages, and debugging running containers.

debug-cluster.md.title: Troubleshooting Clusters
debug-cluster.md.summary: This document provides guidance on troubleshooting Kubernetes clusters, covering how to list nodes, debug down or unreachable nodes, and examine logs for cluster health.

debug.md.title: Monitoring, Logging, and Debugging Guide
debug.md.summary: This guide provides resources for gathering information and resolving issues related to application debugging, cluster troubleshooting, logging, and monitoring within Kubernetes. It directs users to various community forums for further assistance.

deployment.md.title: Kubernetes Deployment Management
deployment.md.summary: This document explains how to use Kubernetes Deployments to manage the desired state of Pods and ReplicaSets. It covers creating, updating, rolling back, scaling, and managing the status of deployments.

device-plugin.md.title: Device Plugin
device-plugin.md.summary: Device plugins run on worker nodes to provide Pods with access to infrastructure resources, like local hardware, that need vendor-specific setup. They advertise these resources to the kubelet so workloads can utilize hardware features.

device-plugins.md.title: Device Plugins
device-plugins.md.summary: This document explains the Kubernetes device plugin framework, allowing vendors to advertise system hardware resources like GPUs or NICs to the kubelet. It details the registration process, resource advertising, and how users request these extended resources in Pod specifications.

device.md.title: Definition of a Device
device.md.summary: This document defines what a 'Device' is within the infrastructure context. It explains that devices are infrastructure resources attached to nodes, such as GPUs or custom hardware, which require drivers for Kubernetes Pods to access them.

deviceclass.md.title: DeviceClass
deviceclass.md.summary: A DeviceClass is a category of cluster devices that can be used with dynamic resource allocation. Administrators use DeviceClasses to define device sets that can be claimed for workloads.

disruption.md.title: Kubernetes Pod Disruptions
disruption.md.summary: This document defines what a disruption is in Kubernetes, which occurs when one or more Pods go out of service. It distinguishes between voluntary disruptions caused by operator actions and involuntary disruptions caused by node or zone failures.

dns-pod-service.md.title: DNS for Services and Pods
dns-pod-service.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes creates DNS records for Services and Pods to enable service discovery. It details how namespaces affect DNS queries and the types of DNS records used for Services and Pods.
